newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Reuter executive urges prompt EMU decisions.
newsitem.headline: Reuter executive urges prompt EMU decisions.

text.p: The European Union would be best advised to speed technical decisions on economic and monetary union if it wanted businesses to be well prepared, Andre Villeneuve, executive director of Reuters said on Monday.

Speaking at a news conference to launch a new book by Reuters on monetary union, called "EMU Explained", Villeneuve said: "Financial markets will lack vital data bases for trading if some key practical decisions are not taken soon."
Among them, Villeneuve urged clarification of how public holidays and settlement dates for securities transactions will be treated under EMU.
Within the 15-nation EU bloc, public holidays vary considerably, a fact that would make accounting for financial transactions more complex under a common currency.
In addition, the technical expertise required to develop computer systems to handle such issues is limited, he added.
Information and technology experts have repeatedly warned businesses to invest early in preparing for the changeover to EMU due to the limited supply of computer programmers.
Villeneuve also noted that information about Europe's planned single currency appeared to be less widespread in Asia than in Europe or the United States.

"Most Asians don't understand why European authorites have not taken more trouble to come out to them and explain why the euro will be a credible currency," he said. -- Brussels newsroom 32 2 287 6838
